_meta.description: What authored text the v2 renderer needs. The words themselves live in the shared callout registry under module 'tabs' and are edited in the Callout Editor; this file is the renderer's contract with them. Validated at build time by report_text.R — a key here with no entry in the registry, or a placeholder in the registry that is not declared here, refuses the build.
_meta.format: key -> { page, context, tokens }. page groups the entry in the Callout Editor and should match a v2 tab. context says where on that tab it renders, so an author knows what they are changing. tokens lists the {placeholders} the renderer supplies for that key, and token_help says in plain English what each one becomes — the Callout Editor shows that beside the text being edited; any other {lower_snake_case} in the authored text is a typo and refuses the build.
_meta.authoring:
Text is the CONTENT of its block — the renderer supplies the surrounding

/

and the data-txt-key tag. Inline markup is limited to strong em b i br p ul ol li h3 h4 span code sup sub, balanced, with no attributes. Blank text renders nothing at all, which is how an author switches a block off without touching code.

report.construction.produced.context: The attribution sentence. Used two ways: on its own in front of a study's own _REPORT_CONSTRUCTION note, and as {producer} inside the stock note below — so it is worded once and correct in both.

token_help.company: the producing company, from company_name in the config's Settings sheet

report.construction.prior_waves_publishe.context: The earlier-waves sentence, dropped into the stock note at {waves_note}. Separate because only the build knows when it is true: the report must carry earlier waves and none of them may hold respondent-level scores, since a wave with scores IS recalculated.

conf.footer.range_meaning_rerun.context: Precision footer — how the example's range reads without a correction (it describes a re-run).

conf.footer.what_95_means.context: Precision footer — what 95% means. Probability samples only.

token_help.moe_pp: how far its numbers can move, in points

conf.footer.significant_means.context: Precision footer — what 'significant' does and does not claim.

conf.design.non_probability.context: Precision footer, About this survey — a non-probability design; the ranges are stability intervals, not confidence intervals.

conf.fpc.body_sample.context: Precision footer, finite population correction — the sample case, where sampling uncertainty is unchanged because most of the universe was never asked.

report.construction.stock.context: About card — the whole Report construction section, as one entry. Blank lines separate paragraphs. {producer} is the attribution sentence above; {waves_note} is the earlier-waves sentence, which appears only when the report is entitled to claim it — move it to say it elsewhere, delete it to never say it. A study that fills in _REPORT_CONSTRUCTION in its config replaces this entire section.

token_help.producer: the attribution sentence — 'This report was produced by … using Turas Analytics …'. Edited under 'Report construction — attribution'.
token_help.waves_note: the earlier-waves sentence — 'Figures carried forward from earlier waves are shown as previously published rather than recalculated.' Appears only when the report carries earlier waves and none of them holds respondent-level data. Renders as nothing otherwise, leaving no empty paragraph.

cards.sig.explainer.context: The whole 'Understanding the significance testing' panel under every crosstab card, as one entry. Blank lines separate paragraphs. {min_base} is the project's own low-base threshold, so a study configured to something other than 30 is described correctly — keep it rather than typing a number.

token_help.min_base: this project's low-base threshold — the sample a column needs before letters show, e.g. 30

cards.reading.list.context: The whole 'Reading this table' panel under every crosstab card, as one entry — ONE BULLET PER LINE. {legend_link} is the 'How to read this report' button the renderer supplies; keep it where you want the cross-reference to sit.

token_help.legend_link: the 'ⓘ How to read this report' button, which opens the legend panel

filter.weighting.bases.context: The three base sizes a weighted table shows, as one entry — ONE BULLET PER LINE. Follows the lead-in above.

reader.legend.arrows.context: Legend panel, Arrows & change chips — both bullets as one entry, ONE BULLET PER LINE.

reader.legend.bands.context: Legend panel, Score bands — both bullets as one entry, ONE BULLET PER LINE. {bands} is the study's own banding, read off its questions, so it describes what the cards actually show.

token_help.bands: the study's own banding, read off its questions, e.g. 'strong ≥8.6, moderate 8.0–8.5, weak <8.0'
